hints: Focus on the reaction conditions, ethanolic NaOH with heat means elimination to form alkenes, not substitution to alcohols.
Draw out 2-bromopentane and remove H from the carbons next to C2, you can form pent-1-ene from C1 and pent-2-ene from C3.
Check each alkene for E/Z isomerism by looking for two different groups on each C=C carbon, then add up all the distinct structural and stereoisomers.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Great start, let's read the conditions. Ethanolic NaOH with heat favours elimination of HBr to give an alkene.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{C}_5\text{H}_{10} + \text{Br}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the structural isomers**

Now draw 2-bromopentane: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CHBr-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$. Remove Br from C2 plus H from a neighbour.

Remove H from C1 gives pent-1-ene: $\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$. Remove H from C3 gives pent-2-ene: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$. So we have 2 positional isomers.

**Check for stereoisomerism**

This is the clever part. For E/Z isomerism, each C=C carbon must have two different groups.

Pent-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-}$, one carbon has two H atoms, so no E/Z. Pent-2-ene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, both C=C carbons have two different groups, so it exists as E-pent-2-ene and Z-pent-2-ene.

**Count the total hydrocarbons**

Add them up: 1 for pent-1-ene plus 2 for E and Z pent-2-ene.

$$1 + 2 = 3 \text{ different hydrocarbons}$$

options.A: Incorrect. This assumes only one elimination product forms, ignoring that H can be removed from either C1 or C3 to give both pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene.
options.B: Incorrect. This correctly counts the two structural isomers, pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene, but forgets stereoisomerism. Pent-2-ene can exist as E and Z forms, so there is one more.
options.C: Correct. Elimination gives pent-1-ene (1 isomer, no E/Z) and pent-2-ene (2 isomers, E and Z). Total is 3 different hydrocarbon alkenes.
options.D: Incorrect. This is the common overcount trap. It assumes both alkenes show E/Z isomerism to give 2 + 2 = 4. In fact pent-1-ene has $\text{CH}_2\text{=}$ with two identical H atoms, so it shows no stereoisomerism.
